subject: Service obligation boundaries & nightly patch-window clarity
body:
From: Sarah West <sarah.west@skyline.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Cho <kyle.cho@skyline.io>, procurement@skyline.io
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA + order form — support & patch-window clarifications

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the MSA + order form earlier this week. Procurement and engineering reviewed and we have a handful of redline asks focused on the support commitments and maintenance/patch language before we can move to legal sign-off. High-level items:

- "Patch window" wording looks broader than what our infra team expects — we need explicit per-region times and an annual max on total weekly patch time (to limit user impact).
- Emergency vs scheduled: procurement wants scheduled windows to have >=72h notice and a rolling canary approach for global customers. For emergency patches we need a defined notification SLA and audit evidence.
- Response tiers: P1/P0 response and remediation timelines in the order form are not aligned with our internal on-call obligations. Can Redwood confirm P1 acknowledge <=30 min and target mitigation ETA?
- Credits: we understand credits are available, but want a clear cap (monthly % or dollar cap) and a formula tied to measured downtime per region.

I've attached our procurement schedule and a short note from eng on acceptable patch durations. Can you do a first-pass redline and loop in legal? Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah

--
Sarah West
Head of Procurement, Skyline Health
sarah.west@skyline.io
(415) 555-0123

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah West <sarah.west@skyline.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + order form — support & patch-window clarifications

Sarah — thanks for the clear notes, this is helpful. Quick summary / proposed approach from our side:

1) Definitions: we will split the contract language into two discrete terms: "Scheduled Maintenance Window" (planned, announced) and "Patch Window" (short-duration rolling patches and security fixes). We'll add a definition section to the order form so both are unambiguous.

2) Window timing & cap: propose default nightly patch window of 02:00–05:00 PT per region (customer may request alternate regional windows). To address your ask for a weekly cap, propose: "Total cumulative Patch Window time will not exceed 3 hours per calendar week per region unless expressly agreed in writing."

3) Notification: scheduled maintenance — >=72 hours notice; emergency patches — we will notify as soon as action is required and provide a post-incident audit. For emergency notification SLA we propose initial acknowledgement to the customer channel within 60 minutes of detection and a follow-up status within 4 hours.

4) Credits: propose a simple cap: monthly service credit not to exceed 10% of monthly service fees for downtime attributable to Redwood, with the credit calculated proportionally by region and downtime minutes. For very short rolling patches (<=30 minutes per region) we propose no credit.

5) Response times: we can commit to the following order-form response ladder for supported tiers (subject to the purchased support package): P0/P1 — initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes during business hours; target mitigation ETA depends on severity and will be listed in the order form as ranges (we'll draft specific minutes/hours for each severity).

6) Canary / rollouts: we'll include a clause that major changes affecting global routing will be introduced via staged canary rollouts and that customers with Dedicated/Private deployments will get pre-cutover test windows.

I've attached our first redline (Redwood_Redline_MSA_v2.docx) with these proposals called out. Laura — can you please review the draft redline and comment on any legal exposure, specifically around the "no credit for <=30 min" carveout and the weekly cap?

Next steps: Laura reviews redline by EOD tomorrow; Marissa to schedule a 30-min call with Sarah + Kyle + our eng lead to align on the weekly cap and canary approach.

Best,
Irene

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah West <sarah.west@skyline.io>, Kyle Cho <kyle.cho@skyline.io>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + order form — support & patch-window clarifications

All — reviewed the Redwood_Redline_MSA_v2.docx and added legal comments (attached). High-level items from Legal:

- The "no credit for <=30 minutes" carveout is risky if repeated frequently; propose changing it to: "Downtime attributable to Patch Windows that individually do not exceed 30 minutes will not individually trigger a credit; however, if cumulative downtime attributable to Patch Windows exceeds 60 minutes in a single calendar day for the same region, the customer may be eligible for credit under the standard credit formula."

- For emergency maintenance, we should avoid an absolute "no credit" stance. Instead, require Redwood to provide timely audit evidence (logs, KV cache snapshots, and request traces) before any credit is paid; also add an audit window and rights to request deeper post-incident reports.

- Add a narrowly tailored SLA carveout for security-critical patches where immediate action is necessary; limit the carveout by requiring a documented risk assessment and CISO-level sign-off internally.

- Suggest adding a mutual review clause for rolling canaries: customer may opt-out of the canary on a per-release basis with advance notice, but Redwood retains right to require canary for safety/security reasons.

I attached a pdf with inline comments (legal_comments_MSA.pdf). Two asks for the customer: please confirm whether your teams consider "region" to be per cloud region (e.g., us-west-1) or per legal customer footprint (global). That affects how we calculate regional credits.

Irene/Marissa — once Sarah confirms region semantics and accepts the credit thresholds we can finalize redlines and route to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

[Attachment: legal_comments_MSA.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sarah West <sarah.west@skyline.io>

Cc: Kyle Cho <kyle.cho@skyline.io>, procurement@skyline.io
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + order form — support & patch-window clarifications

Irene / Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed redline. A few concise responses from our side:

- Region semantics: Skyline will treat "region" as the cloud region (e.g., us-west-2). That keeps crediting tied to actual impacted locality.
- Weekly cap: 3 hours/week per region sounds workable, provided we get clear calendar entries for scheduled patches and pre-cutover runbooks for canaries.
- Credit carveout: we can accept the revised language Laura suggested (thresholds and cumulative aggregation). Please ensure the credit calculation example is included in the order form (minutes down -> % of monthly fee) so procurement can sign off.
- Response tiers: Our P1 expectation is acknowledgement <=30 min and an initial mitigation plan within 2 hours; P2 acknowledgement within 4 hours. If you can map Redwood's proposed ranges into a small table we can accept it and move to DocuSign.

Next step for us: Marissa / Irene, please circulate the revised redline with Laura's wording incorporated and include an illustrative credit calc row in the order form. We can turn that around in 48 business hours.

Irene — please also include links to the post-incident audit template you mentioned.

Thanks,
Sarah

--

Head of Procurement, Skyline Health
